simple.meaning: דְּמָמָה (dᵉmâmâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “quiet.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דְּמָמָה (H1827) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 19:12, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Job, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דְּמָמָה (H1827) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דְּמָמָה (H1827) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דְּמָמָה (dᵉmâmâh) / H1827 is traced through 1 Kings 19:12, Job 4:16, Psalms 107:29 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1827. demamah דְּמָמָה noun feminine (silence) whisper (on formation compare Ba NB 87 ) — דַקָּ֑ה דְּמָמָה קוֺל הָאֵשׁ וְאַחַר 1Kin 19:12 ; אֶשְׁמָ֑ע זָקוֺל דְּמָמָה Job 4:16 a whisper and a voice, i.e. an articulate whisper (compare Di); לִדְמָמָ֑ה סְעָרָה יָקֵם Psa 107:29 he settleth storm into whisper.

occurrences.englishText: After the earthquake a fire passed; but Yahweh was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.
It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance.
